---
title: "CLI Guide"
---

The per-command reference (arguments, options, `--help` text) is generated from
the Typer app and lives under **Reference → CLI**. This page covers what the
help text cannot: how the commands compose, what they print as JSON, exit
codes, and environment.

```
tether init [PATH]
tether add KEY [LOCATOR] --kind KIND [--branch BRANCH] [--at STATE | --pick] [locator options] [--set k=v]... [--file immutable|versioned] [--pin native|record]
tether set KEY... | --all [--file immutable|versioned] [--pin native|record]
tether remove KEY
tether status [--snapshot | --no-snapshot]
tether snapshot
tether pull [BOOKMARK] [-m MESSAGE]
tether commit -m MESSAGE [--no-vcs] [--strict] [--force] [--no-snapshot] [--dry-run | --plan FILE]
tether commit --from-plan FILE [-m MESSAGE] [--no-vcs]
tether new [REV] [-b NAME] [--shared] [--keep] [--eager | --lazy] [--discard] [--dry-run | --plan FILE | --from-plan FILE]
tether open KEY [-r REV] [--read-only | --writable]
tether restore KEY... --from REV [--discard] [--dry-run | --plan FILE | --from-plan FILE]
tether promote [KEY]... [-r REV] [--strategy auto|ff|merge] [-m MESSAGE] [--dry-run | --plan FILE | --from-plan FILE]
tether verify [-r REV] [--all-history] [--deep]
tether diff [REV_A] [REV_B] [--content] [--limit N]
tether log KEY [--ref REF] [-n N]            # or: tether log LOCATOR --kind KIND [--branch B] [--set k=v]
tether gc [--dry-run | --no-dry-run] [--prune-bookmarks [--keep-bookmark NAME]... [--force-prune]] [--plan FILE | --from-plan FILE]
tether abandon REV... [--gc]
tether forget-workspace [WORKSPACE_ID] [--dry-run | --plan FILE | --from-plan FILE]
tether ops [-n N]
tether undo [OP_ID | --to OP_ID] [--discard]
tether repair [--all-history] [--dry-run | --plan FILE | --from-plan FILE]
tether upgrade [--ignore-immutable] [--dry-run | --plan FILE | --from-plan FILE]
tether export PATH [--rev REV]... [--format sqlite|parquet|csv|jsonl] [--listings] [--workspace] [--append]
tether publish [--to DSN] [--schema NAME] [--rev REV]... [--listings] [--dry-run]
tether import SOURCE [--table NAME | --query SQL] [--sync] [--dry-run | --plan FILE | --from-plan FILE]
```

Commands run from anywhere inside a dataset: the root is found by walking up to
the nearest `tether.toml`. Every command that inspects external systems fans out
concurrently across objects, and every command that prints a result accepts
`--json`.

## Exit codes and errors

`0` on success, `1` on any `TetherError` (printed to stderr as `error: ...`).
`verify` also exits `1` when any report is not `ok`, which makes it a natural
CI gate. `undo`, `repair`, and `upgrade` exit `2` when they did part of the job and the
store would not allow the rest (each such part is printed as `IRREVERSIBLE` /
`FAILED`). Failures in one object's backend during a fan-out are aggregated
into one message listing each object.

## Revisions

`REV` arguments are passed to the enclosing VCS untouched: jj revsets (`@`,
`@-`, `main`, change ids) in a jj repository, git revisions (`HEAD~2`, tags,
shas) in a git repository. A `REV` that names a bookmark (jj) or branch (git)
is one tether works on; `tether new REV` for any other revision gives a
read-only working copy. In git that commit is checked out onto a
`tether/<rev12>` branch so the dataset commits you make there stay reachable
(a detached HEAD would let `gc` treat them as gone); those `tether/*` branches
are parking, not bookmarks -- tether never deletes them, so `git branch -d`
the ones you are done with.

## Environment

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `TETHER_REV` | Default `--rev` for `open`: handles resolve read-only at that commit's pinned state. Set it in reproducible jobs. |
| `PATH`, `JJ_CONFIG` | Used by the `jj` / `git` executables tether shells out to (also configurable via `[vcs] jj_path` / `git_path`). |
| Backend credentials | Never stored in manifests; each backend reads them from the environment (`NEON_API_KEY`, `DOLT_PASSWORD`, AWS/GCP/Azure defaults, lakeFS `LAKECTL_*`, ...). See [Backends](09-backends.qmd). |

## Locator options for `add`

The positional `LOCATOR` becomes the `uri` field. Named options map to locator
fields; `--set key=value` (repeatable) covers everything else. Which fields a
backend reads is listed per backend in [Backends](09-backends.qmd).

| Option | Locator field | Typical backends |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LOCATOR` (positional) | `uri` | file, icechunk, delta, lance, ducklake (`metadata`) |
| `--branch` | `branch` | icechunk, neon, iceberg, lance, lakefs, dolt: the object's *upstream* (default `main`) -- what the trunk bookmark stands for: the first commit pins it, a trunk `pull` reads it, `promote` lands on it |
| `--project-id`, `--database`, `--role` | same | neon; `--database` also dolt |
| `--remote` | `remote` | git (push pins to a remote) |
| `--region` | `region` | file (object stores), icechunk, delta |
| `--repository`, `--prefix` | same | lakefs |
| `--host`, `--port` | same | dolt |
| `--table` | `table` | ducklake (handle scope), iceberg (alias of `identifier`) |
| `--at ID` / `--pick` | `at` | initial position: snapshot id / version / commit / tag (all but file, neon) that the first commit pins instead of the branch head; `--pick` chooses from `log` interactively |
| `--set k=v` | `k` | `path=`, `identifier=`, `data_path=`, `allow_dirty=1`, ... |

`tether set KEY... --file|--pin` changes a registered object's policy in
place (`--all` for every object): manifest-only, logged, undoable. Commit to
record the policy. Whether writes fork or land upstream is not a policy: it is
the bookmark the working copy is on.

Policy options: `--file immutable|versioned` (`file` only: treat drift
as an error, or record object-store version ids), `--pin native|record` (any
backend: create a native ref per commit, or record the state only and fork
from it while the system retains it -- see
[Reclaiming storage](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd)).

## Status labels

```
dataset 3f9c2a1b7d0e (STALE); on bookmark relabel
       new  raw/plate1  [file/observed] unrecoverable
  modified  zarr/imaging  [icechunk/forkable]
     clean  db/metrics  [neon/forkable] verify=ok
```

- The header names the bookmark this working copy is on (`on trunk bookmark
  main`; `on no bookmark: read-only`), and a `warning:` line follows when the
  VCS moved, renamed, or deleted it behind tether's back, with what to do.
- `new` never committed; `modified` current state differs from the committed
  one; `clean` unchanged; `error` the fingerprint failed.
- `unrecoverable`: the committed state cannot be reconstructed later (Observed).
- `(STALE)`: HEAD's manifests changed since this workspace forked its refs;
  run `tether new` before writing.
- `verify=`: shown when `[verify] on_status = true`.

`status` is local by default: it shows the *last* snapshot of each object's
state and prints its age (`states as fingerprinted 2h ago; --snapshot to
refresh`), contacting nothing -- like `jj status`, it is meant to be cheap
enough to run constantly. `--snapshot` fans out and fingerprints every object
first: one metadata round-trip per system in parallel, so wall time is the
slowest one (a suspended Neon compute has to wake). A workspace with no
snapshot yet always takes one. `[snapshot] auto = true` makes every `status`
fingerprint; `--no-snapshot` then wins. `verify` always fingerprints.

States: `new` (no commit yet), `modified` (the bookmark's branch for the
object differs from the commit), `behind` (on the trunk, a branch-less or
`--at` object whose system moved past its pin -- `pull` takes it), `clean`,
`error`. A commit refreshes the cache only for the objects it fingerprinted,
so an object a fan-out found `behind` still reads `behind` after an unrelated
commit. See [Positions](04-branching-and-writing.qmd#positions-and-tether-pull).

## What `pull` does

The dataset's fetch. For the bookmark this working copy is on (the only one
it can pull; `tether new NAME` first for another): fingerprint the heads of
its branches -- on the trunk, every object's upstream branch (`locator.branch`,
ignoring `at`) and, for systems without branches, the object itself; on any
other bookmark, its `tether.ws.*` branches -- and, where that differs from the
bookmark's commit, pin it and commit on the bookmark, which moves. Nothing
moved: no commit. Objects not yet committed, and objects whose branch does not
exist yet, are skipped with a reason; a `file = "immutable"` object that
changed is refused; uncommitted manifest edits are refused (commit them
first). `undo` uncommits a pull like a commit.

## What `commit` does

1. Refuse if the VCS working copy has left the bookmark (`status` says how to
   return). Under jj the bookmark must be on the working copy or its parent
   -- where `new` and `commit` leave it; a `jj new` past an empty change puts
   it a step further back, and `commit` refuses rather than move it in a
   second operation (`tether new NAME --keep` brings the working copy back
   without touching branches). Snapshot the bookmark's branches -- on the trunk every upstream
   branch, elsewhere the `tether.ws.*` branches that exist -- unless
   `--no-snapshot`. Objects with no branch keep their pin. Then quiescence
   checks for backends that need them (Neon refuses while writers are active;
   `--force` skips).
2. For each object whose state changed: Pinnable/Forkable backends create the
   native ref `tether.<pin_id>`; Addressable and `--pin record` objects record
   the state; Observed backends record it with `recoverable = false`
   (`--strict` fails instead). Unchanged objects are skipped.
3. Write `.tether/objects/<key>.toml` and any `.tether/listings/<hash>.jsonl`,
   then `jj commit` / `git commit` scoped to those paths (`--no-vcs` skips).
4. Move the bookmark onto the new commit (one jj operation with the commit,
   so `jj undo` takes both back; git branches follow by themselves). The
   store branches stay where they are: `commit` is not `jj commit`, nothing
   new is forked, and the next write lands on the same branch.

## What `new` does

Decides which bookmark this working copy works on, then records a working ref
per Forkable object. `-b NAME` creates the bookmark at `REV` (default: here)
-- refused if it exists; `REV` naming a bookmark joins it; any other `REV`
takes the bookmark at that commit (the one this workspace has, else the
trunk, else the only one) or, if none, makes the working copy read-only; no
`REV` keeps the current bookmark. A bookmark another live checkout works on is
refused unless `--shared`. On the trunk (`[vcs] trunk`, default `main`) the
working ref is each object's upstream branch (`trunk` in the plan); on any
other bookmark it is `tether.ws.<dataset>.<bookmark>` in that object's system.
By default (`[new] fork = "lazy"`) that branch is *not created yet* -- the plan
shows `defer-fork` and the first writable `open` creates it from the pin.
`--eager` creates them all during `new`. Objects with `pin = "record"` fork
during `new` regardless, because only a branch keeps their recorded state from
expiring. `Repo.materialize_fork(key)` creates one deferred branch on demand.
The trade-offs are laid out in [Branching and writing](04-branching-and-writing.qmd#lazy-or-eager).

A working branch this workspace already has is *reset* onto the pin by the
fork -- unless it already sits exactly at the pin (you just committed from
it), in which case the plan says `reuse` and the branch is kept as is. If its
head holds writes that were never committed, the plan shows a `refuse` action
and `new` stops before touching the VCS or any store; commit the writes, or
pass `--discard` to throw them away (the fork action then says what it
discards).

If a pin fails, pins created by the same commit are released best-effort.

## Plans: `--dry-run`, `--plan`, `--from-plan`

`commit`, `new`, `gc`, `promote`, `import`, and `repair` are the commands that
write to external systems, and each is a plan followed by an apply. `--dry-run` runs only the plan and prints
it (as JSON with `--json`); `--plan FILE` also saves it; `--from-plan FILE`
skips planning and applies the saved actions. Before applying, tether
re-fingerprints the planned objects (and, for `new`, re-reads the manifests at
the target) and refuses with `StalePlanError` if anything differs from what
the plan recorded. `gc` is a dry run unless `--no-dry-run` or `--from-plan` is
given.

```
plan: commit (2 write(s))
                 pin  zarr/imaging  [icechunk] tether.0a1b2c3d.deb4861eb388e5f6  native ref at snapshot_id=K3F9M2A1B7C8D4E5…
          vcs-commit  jj commit: 'Relabel plate1'
                      db/metrics: unchanged
```

Action verbs: `pin`, `record` (commit); `fork`, `defer-fork`, `reuse`, `trunk` (new);
`fork`, `refuse` (restore); `delete-branch`, `keep-branch`, `delete-file`, `forget-vcs-workspace` (forget-workspace); `fast-forward`, `merge`, `refuse` (promote); `unpin`,
`delete-branch`, `keep-branch`, `forget-working-ref`, `delete-listing` (gc);
`add`, `update`, `remove` (import); `upsert` (publish); `repin`, `refork`
(repair); `rename-pin`, `rename-branch`, `rewrite-history` (upgrade);
`vcs-commit`. `trunk`, `defer-fork`, `reuse`, `refuse`, and `keep-branch` are
informational -- they write nothing.

## `gc` scope

Default: release pins no manifest in VCS history (or the working tree)
references, forget the working refs of objects removed with `tether remove`
(the native branch is left alone), and delete unreferenced
`.tether/listings/` files. No branch is ever deleted by a plain `gc`.

`--prune-bookmarks` also sweeps `tether.ws.*` branches: those of bookmarks
that are gone (every bookmark the VCS has, or a live checkout works on, is
kept; `--keep-bookmark NAME` keeps one that only exists elsewhere), legacy
per-workspace branches from before bookmarks, and this bookmark's branches
that no current object uses. Each branch gets one verdict:

| Branch head | Default | `--force-prune` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| natively pinned by some commit, or equal to the base branch | `delete-branch` | `delete-branch` |
| holds unpinned writes | `keep-branch` | `delete-branch FORCED` (data lost) |
| a `--pin record` state (no native ref) | `keep-branch` | `delete-branch FORCED` |
| on a `BRANCH_IS_STORAGE` backend (Neon) | `keep-branch` | `delete-branch FORCED` |
| the store refuses to delete it (Neon: pins hang off it) | `keep-branch: cannot be deleted` | same |

Both sweeps stay inside this dataset's namespace: pins and branches whose
name carries another dataset's id are counted in the plan's notes (`N pin(s)
of other datasets left alone`) and never touched, `--force-prune` included.

## `abandon`

`tether abandon REV...` is `jj abandon` / a git rebase that drops the commits,
plus the `gc` plan for the pins only they referenced. Later commits keep
their manifests exactly as they were (snapshot, not patch, semantics -- the
VCS's own rebase would conflict on them). Nothing is released unless `--gc`;
`tether gc --no-dry-run` does it later. Under git the commits must be on the
current branch and the tree clean; a conflict outside `.tether/` aborts. Not
undoable by tether -- `jj undo` / the reflog bring the commits back, `repair`
the pins.

## `forget-workspace`

`tether forget-workspace [ID]` (default: this one) is `jj workspace forget` /
`git worktree remove` plus tether's half: its `workspace.toml` and `ops.jsonl`
are removed and the VCS stops tracking the checkout. Store branches belong to
bookmarks, not workspaces, so none are touched -- `jj bookmark delete NAME`
then `gc --prune-bookmarks` releases them. Forgetting the current workspace
leaves the directory without a working copy under jj, as `jj workspace
forget` does. Plan/apply; not undoable. The retire-a-bookmark flow:
[Reclaiming storage](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd#branches-of-bookmarks-that-are-gone).

## `ops`, `undo`, `repair`

Every command that writes to a store appends an entry to this workspace's
operation log, `.tether/ops.jsonl` (untracked; see
[Concepts](02-concepts.qmd#the-operation-log)). `tether ops` prints the newest
entries, one line each -- id, time, command, what it did, and `(undone by ID)`
where applicable.

`tether undo [OP_ID]` reverses the newest undoable entry (or the one named):

```
$ tether undo
undid 3f1c9a2b7d4e (new: forked db, zarr/imaging)
  restored   db: deleted tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel
  restored   zarr/imaging: deleted tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel
  restored   workspace.toml restored
```

| Undoing a... | Does | Refused when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `commit` | uncommits it (jj: squash into `@`; git: `reset --soft`); manifests become working-tree edits; pins stay | it is no longer the working copy's parent |
| `new`, lazy fork | deletes branches it created, re-points branches it reset to their recorded heads, restores `workspace.toml`, returns the VCS working copy if it has not moved, deletes a bookmark `-b` made | a branch gained writes since (commit them, or `--discard`) |
| `pull` | uncommits it like a `commit`; pins stay | it is no longer the working copy's parent |
| `gc` | recreates deleted branches and listings; deleted *pins* cannot come back and print as `IRREVERSIBLE` (exit `2`) | -- |
| `add`, `remove`, `import` | restores the manifests | -- |
| `promote` | -- | always; the previous upstream heads are printed (the trunk bookmark: `jj bookmark set main -r <before>`) |
| `repair`, `upgrade`, `abandon`, `forget-workspace` | -- | always |

When the VCS goes around tether (`jj undo`, `jj abandon`, `git reset` on a
dataset commit), `tether status` prints a `warning:` per vanished commit and
`tether ops` flags its entry `(vcs commit gone)`. An *undone* commit leaves the
manifests as uncommitted edits -- commit again; an *abandoned* one reverts
them -- `gc` releases its pins, `repair` recreates them if it comes back.

`tether undo --to OP_ID` undoes every newer operation, newest first, and stops
-- keeping what it already reversed -- at the first it cannot undo. It is not
`jj op restore`: tether's log holds per-op deltas, not whole views, so the walk
is stepwise. Exit `2` unless every step was complete.

`tether repair` rebuilds what the manifests promise: a pin whose native ref is
missing is recreated from the recorded state (if the store still has it); a
working branch this workspace expects but the store lost is forked again.
`--all-history` checks every commit's pins, not just the working tree's. Pins
that exist but point elsewhere are reported as notes, never overwritten. It is
a plan/apply command like the others.

One store will not cooperate: Icechunk keeps a tombstone for every deleted tag
and never lets the name be reused, so a deleted Icechunk pin cannot come back
under its id -- `repair` reports the failure (exit `2`). The recorded snapshot
is still readable while the store has it: `open --rev` and `new` fall back to
it when the tag is gone.

## `upgrade`

`tether.toml` carries `[tether] version`. A dataset made by an older tether is
refused by every command except `upgrade` (and the error says so). `tether
upgrade` runs every pending migration in order -- each takes the dataset from
version `n-1` to `n` and writes the new version before the next starts, so an
interrupted upgrade resumes where it stopped.

```
$ tether upgrade --dry-run
plan: upgrade (5 write(s))
          rename-pin  db  [icechunk] tether.0a1b2c3d.7d1e0c9a2b34e5f6  from tether.7d1e0c9a2b34
          rename-pin  db  [icechunk] tether.0a1b2c3d.c48b2f6e1d07a9b0  from tether.c48b2f6e1d07
       rename-branch  db  [icechunk] tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.7c1e0a4d.db-61a22c  from tether.ws.7c1e0a4d.db
     rewrite-history      3 commit(s)  manifests with old-format pins get the new names; commit ids change, every clone must re-sync
          vcs-commit      tether upgrade: v1 -> v2 (dataset-namespaced refs)
                          dataset id: 0a1b2c3d
```

| Version | Migration | Touches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v2 | dataset id; every pin and working branch renamed into its namespace (the branches keep their pre-bookmark per-workspace names, which `gc --prune-bookmarks` judges as legacy) | stores and history |
| v3 | local `file` states become content hashes (one read per file; the stat cache remembers); the `write` policy line is dropped -- whether writes fork or land upstream is the bookmark now | working tree only |

A migration that renames native refs (v2) has to rewrite history too: `gc`
subtracts what history references from what the stores hold, and both sides
must agree. That means:

- Commit ids change (jj keeps change ids; bookmarks and branches follow).
  Every other clone re-syncs afterwards: `jj git fetch`, or a force-push and
  reset under git.
- Under jj, commits marked immutable (pushed `main`) are only rewritten with
  `--ignore-immutable`.
- It fails **closed**: the dataset id is written first, then the store
  renames; the first failed rename stops the upgrade with history and
  manifests still naming the old refs, so nothing is orphaned.
- Re-running `tether upgrade` continues under the same id and skips the
  renames already made.

## What `restore` does

`tether restore KEY... --from REV` is the per-object `jj restore --from`: it
resets (or creates) `KEY`'s working branch from what `REV`'s manifest pinned
and touches nothing else -- other objects' branches, the working-tree
manifests, and the VCS working copy stay. The object is *not* stale
afterwards: the next `commit` pins what you restored. Its fork point moves to
`REV`'s state, so `promote` treats a base that moved since as a divergence
(merge or refuse), not a fast-forward. A branch holding writes you never
committed is refused unless `--discard`; `undo` puts the branch back to the
head it had. Plan/apply like the others.

## What `promote` does

Per Forkable object, compares the upstream branch to the fork point recorded
when the bookmark's branch was created (or, with `--rev`, to the target's
ancestry): unchanged and `PROMOTE` -> `fast-forward`; moved and `MERGE` ->
`merge`; otherwise `refuse` with the backend's recipe. `--strategy ff` turns
merges into refusals, `--strategy merge` turns fast-forwards into refusals.
When everything fast-forwarded and nothing was refused, the trunk bookmark is
moved to this bookmark's commit (`main -> <commit>` in the output). After a
merge the branch is reset onto the merge result so the next `commit` pins it,
and a second `promote` moves the trunk. Exit status is `1` when anything was
refused (conflicts included) so CI notices. See
[Branching and writing](04-branching-and-writing.qmd#landing-it-tether-promote).

## What `open` prints

| Handle | Address |
| --- | --- |
| `FileHandle` | `uri[#version_id]` |
| `NeonHandle` | connection URL |
| `GitHandle` | `path@sha` |
| `IcechunkHandle` | `uri#<tag or branch or snapshot_id>` |
| `IcebergHandle` | `identifier#<ref or snapshot_id>` |
| `DeltaHandle` | `uri@vN` |
| `LanceHandle` | `uri#tag` or `uri#branch@vN` |
| `LakeFSHandle` | `lakefs://repo/ref/prefix/` |
| `DuckLakeHandle` | `metadata#snapshot=N` |
| `DoltHandle` | `mysql://user@host:port/db/ref` |

Without `-r` (and without `TETHER_REV`), Forkable objects open **writable** at
their working ref -- creating it first if `new` deferred the fork, the one
store write outside `commit` / `new` / `gc` -- and everything else read-only at
the base. With `-r REV`, the
handle is read-only at that commit's pinned (or recorded Addressable) state.

## `log`

Lists an object's native history newest first: id, timestamp, message, and
the branches, tags, and tether pins (`tether.<id>`) pointing at each entry.
For a registered object it starts at the working ref (or the `at` it was
registered at); `--ref` starts elsewhere (a branch, tag, or id). With `--kind`, the
positional is a locator for an unregistered object, so you can browse before
`add`. Ids are valid `--at` values.

## `diff` defaults

No arguments: current commit vs working tree. One revision: that revision vs
nothing (everything `removed`). Two: `REV_A → REV_B`. `--content` adds each
changed object's native diff; `--limit` caps entries printed per object
(counts stay exact).

## `export`, `publish`, `import`

The registry commands are covered in [Registries and SQL](10-registries-and-sql.qmd).
In short: `export` writes the derived tables to a SQLite file (default) or a
directory of parquet / csv / jsonl files; `publish` upserts them into a
Postgres schema (DSN from `--to` or `$TETHER_PUBLISH_DSN`, never
`tether.toml`) and skips commits already present; `import` reads rows with the
canonical object columns from a Postgres DSN, SQLite file, `.csv`, or `.jsonl`
and plans `add` / `update` / `remove` (`--sync`) on the manifests. `import` is
a planned command like `commit`, `new`, and `gc`; `publish --dry-run` prints
per-table counts.

## JSON output

| Command | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| `init` | `{"root": "<absolute path>", "dataset_id": "<8 hex>"}` |
| `status` | `{"manifest_hash", "stale", "stale_keys", "fresh", "snapshot_at", "vcs_drift": [{"op", "commit", "referenced": {key: bool}}], "objects": [{"key", "kind", "tier", "state", "pinned", "recoverable", "verify"}]}`; `fresh` is false when the cached snapshot from `snapshot_at` was shown |
| `snapshot` | `{key: state}` |
| `commit` | `{"vcs_commit": sha or null, "pinned": {key: ref or null}, "unrecoverable": [keys], "unchanged": [keys]}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan (below) |
| `new` | `{"working_refs": {key: ref}, "pending_forks": {key: ref}, "fork_points": {key: state}}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan |
| `promote` | `{"fast_forwarded": {key: state}, "merged": {key: state}, "skipped": [keys], "refused": {key: reason}, "conflicts": {key: [units]}}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan |
| `open` | `{"key", "read_only", "address", "type"}` |
| `restore` | `{"from": rev, "working_refs": {key: ref}}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan |
| `verify` | `{label: {"status", "message"}}` with labels `key` or `<commit12>:key` |
| `diff` | `[{"key", "change", "a": pin_id or null, "b": pin_id or null, "detail": ObjectDiff or null, "detail_error": str or null}]` where `ObjectDiff` is `{"summary", "unit", "added", "removed", "modified", "truncated", "note", "entries": [{"path", "change", "detail"}]}` |
| `log` | `[{"id", "when", "message", "refs": [names]}]` |
| `gc` | dry run (default): the plan; after applying: `{"dry_run": false, "unpinned": {kind: [pin_ids]}, "deleted_working_refs": {key: [refs]}, "kept_working_refs": {key: [refs]}, "forgotten_working_refs": {key: [refs]}, "deleted_listings": [names]}` |
| `abandon` | `{"abandoned": [commit ids], "gc_plan": plan, "gc_applied": bool}` |
| `forget-workspace` | `{"workspace": id8, "deleted_working_refs": {key: [refs]}, "kept_working_refs": {key: [refs]}, "removed_files": [paths], "vcs": str or null, "failed": {target: reason}}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan |
| `ops` | `[{"id", "at", "command", "plan", "result", "pre", "undoes", "undone_by", "vcs_commit_gone"}]`, newest first |
| `undo` | `{"undone": op id, "command", "undo_id", "restored": [str], "irreversible": [str], "skipped": [str]}` |
| `undo --to` | `{"to": op id, "undone": [{"op", "command", "undo_id", "restored", "irreversible", "skipped"}], "stopped_at": op id or null, "reason"}` |
| `repair` | `{"repinned": {key: pin_id}, "reforked": {key: ref}, "failed": {target: reason}, "notes": [str]}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan |
| `upgrade` | `{"from_version", "to_version", "renamed_pins": {old ref: new ref}, "renamed_branches": {old: new}, "rewritten_commits": {old id: new id}, "failed": {target: reason}, "vcs_commit"}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan |
| plan | `{"format": 1, "command", "created_at", "context": {...}, "notes": [str], "actions": [{"op", "key", "kind", "target", "detail", "params": {...}}]}` -- what `--plan FILE` writes and `--from-plan` reads |
| `export` | `{"path", "format", "head", "rows": {table: count}}` |
| `publish` | `{"schema", "head", "upserted": {table: count}, "skipped_commits"}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan (one `upsert` action per table) |
| `import` | `{"added": [keys], "updated": [keys], "removed": [keys], "unchanged": [keys]}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan |
